Workshop note, Tuesday evening session, Ward 12 Community Centre. Written by Nirmala, facilitator.
Tonight we looked at ads on phones. Shreya, one of our regular participants, offered to show how she checks a post before believing it. She opened a video of a creator praising a hair oil. First she tapped the name and found the small "paid partnership" label. Then she searched for the oil with the word "review" and read two long reviews from people who were not selling anything. One said it was fine, nothing special.
She also pointed out that the video began with a scare about hair fall. "I didn't have that worry before I watched," she said, and the room laughed. She said she still enjoys the creator's videos.
Next step: I have asked Shreya to lead the first ten minutes next week.

qa.q: What label did Shreya find when she tapped the creator's name?
qa.a: Shreya found the small "paid partnership" label.

qa.q: What does Shreya's joke about hair fall suggest she felt?
qa.a: Shreya felt amused, and a little put off, that the video had planted a worry she did not have; she sees the ad as trying to create a need rather than meet one.

qa.q: Which of Shreya's steps could others copy?
qa.a: Checking for a sponsorship label, reading reviews from people not selling anything, and asking what worry the ad is trying to create before buying.

qa.q: How might the others in the room be affected by Shreya's demonstration?
qa.a: Seeing someone like them check calmly, and still enjoy the videos, may make the steps feel normal and easy rather than suspicious or dull.

grounding: A community workshop facilitator records an adult checking sponsorship, independent reviews and the need an ad creates, while still enjoying the creator.

passage:
14 March, late
Watched Tomas's new travel video tonight. Hilltop cabin, mist, a laptop on a wooden table, him saying this laptop "changed how I work". Honestly, it was beautiful and I watched it twice.
Old me would have opened the shop page. Instead I paused and scrolled down. There it was, "sponsored by", small grey letters under the description.
Then I searched the laptop with "battery problems". Three separate forums, lots of complaints about the hinge. Middle ratings, not the five-star ones, were the useful ones.
Lalremsiami, from the other side of the sofa: "So is it good?"
Me: "The cabin is good. The laptop is paid."
Also noticed: the video never said I needed a new laptop. It just made my old one look sad next to the mist.
Still following him. Still not buying.
Chetan

qa.q: What did Chetan find written under the video's description?
qa.a: Chetan found "sponsored by" in small grey letters under the description.

qa.q: What does Chetan's line "The cabin is good. The laptop is paid." suggest about how Chetan feels?
qa.a: Chetan can enjoy the video's beauty while staying unconvinced by the product, so Chetan feels relaxed and in control rather than steered.

qa.q: Which checking step turned out most useful for Chetan?
qa.a: Searching for battery problems and reading the middle ratings showed complaints about the hinge that the video never mentioned.

qa.q: What might Lalremsiami learn from Chetan's answer?
qa.a: Lalremsiami might see that it is possible to like a creator's video and still separate it from the paid product being shown.

grounding: An adult enjoys a sponsored travel video but checks the label, independent reviews and the need it tries to create, and decides not to buy.

passage:
The van reached Nandgaon's weekly market with its speaker blaring. On a screen tied to its side, a well-known folk singer from the district sang about a pressure cooker: "Quick food, happy home, proud family!"
Seema, who taught at the girls' school, stood humming along. Then she asked the salesman, "Did the singer get paid for this song?"
He grinned. "Of course, madam. Big fee."
"And what happens when the whistle breaks?"
"Service centre in the district town."
That was forty kilometres away. Seema found Ayesha by the bangle stall. "Your Ammi bought one last year, no?"
"Whistle went in three months," Ayesha said. "She uses the old one now."
Walking home, Seema noticed the song never mentioned repairs, only "proud family", as if a good home needed that cooker. She still hummed the tune.

qa.q: How far away was the service centre?
qa.a: The service centre in the district town was forty kilometres away.

qa.q: What was Seema thinking about as she walked home, and how did she feel?
qa.a: Seema felt wary and a little amused; she noticed the song left out repairs and played on the wish to feel like a proud family.

qa.q: Which questions helped Seema see past the song?
qa.a: Asking whether the singer was paid, what happens when the whistle breaks, and checking with Ayesha, whose Ammi had actually bought one.

qa.q: How might the salesman see a customer who asks about repairs?
qa.a: As harder to sell to, since the ad works best when buyers hear only 'happy home' and not the forty-kilometre trip for service.

grounding: Shows an adult asking who paid for an ad, checking with a real buyer, and noticing the need the song creates while still enjoying it.

passage:
Pablo was scrolling on the tram home in Valencia when the video caught him: a creator floating in turquoise water outside a white hotel. "You deserve to disappear for a while. Link in bio." After a week of late shifts, he felt the pull in his chest.
At home he showed Freya. "Look at this place."
"Gorgeous," she said. "Who paid for the stay?"
Pablo tapped the post. Under "more", in small letters: "hosted". He opened a travel forum and read the three-star reviews instead of the five-star ones. Construction next door. Seaweed in August. A nice breakfast.
"It's not a scam," he said. "It's just an ad with nice light."
He noticed the words again: you deserve. The ad wasn't selling a hotel; it was selling rest to a tired person.
He saved the video anyway, because he liked the camera work. Then he booked nothing and went to bed early.

qa.q: What word appeared under 'more' on the post?
qa.a: In small letters, the word 'hosted'.

qa.q: What was Pablo feeling when he first saw the video on the tram?
qa.a: Pablo felt tired and full of longing, a pull in his chest after a week of late shifts, so the escape looked like exactly what he needed.

qa.q: What did Pablo check, and what did it show?
qa.a: He checked who paid and found 'hosted', then read the three-star reviews, which mentioned construction and seaweed that the video left out.

qa.q: What would change if Freya had just said 'Book it'?
qa.a: Pablo might have paid for an escape sold to his tiredness without learning that the stay was hosted or about the construction next door.

grounding: Shows an adult checking who paid for a travel post, reading middling reviews and noticing the ad sells rest to tiredness, while still enjoying it.

passage: In the office pantry, Indu held out her phone to Pranav. "This guy's course will fix your career in thirty days. Everyone on my feed is doing it." Pranav watched the clip: a man in a sunlit flat, laptop open, a speedboat behind him, saying, "If you're stuck in a nine-to-five, you're wasting your life." Pranav smiled; it was a good video. Then he scrolled to the caption. Small grey letters: Sponsored. He searched the course name plus "review" and skipped the first page of glowing posts. On a forum, people wrote that the lessons were free videos repackaged. "So what is he actually selling?" Pranav said. "A course. But first he's selling the feeling that my job is a waste." Indu frowned. "Is it, though?" "Some days," Pranav laughed. "But I didn't think so till I saw the speedboat." He put the kettle on. "Nice video, though. I'll just keep my money."

qa.q: What small grey word appeared in the caption?
qa.a: Sponsored.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling as he watched the clip?
qa.a: Pranav enjoyed it, smiling at a good video, while staying curious and sceptical about who had paid for it.

qa.q: Which checks did Pranav use?
qa.a: He looked for the sponsored label, searched for independent reviews beyond the first glowing page, and noticed the need the ad was trying to create.

qa.q: How might Indu feel after Pranav's comments?
qa.a: Indu seems unsettled, asking whether it is a waste, perhaps wondering if the ad had made her doubt her own job too.

grounding: Shows an adult checking whether a post is sponsored, looking for independent reviews and noticing the need the ad creates, while still enjoying it.
